To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
crystallization in low diffusion gels or in space, in the absence of gravity, can be a powerful tool to prepare high-resolution crystals of proteins.
crystallization in low diffusive gelled media or microgravity environments can improve the quality of the protein crystals and that this is of relevance for structural biology.
aspartyl-tRNAsynthetases are excellent model proteins to study the effect of crystallogenesis conditions on the crystalline quality of protein crystals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of methods that improve the intrinsic physical properties of protein crystals.
the physical properties of protein crystals, their crystallization, and crystal quality, and with the use of space to improve crystal quality.
the crystallizability and crystalline quality of a protein family.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
space-grown protein crystals can be better than those grown in the laboratory.
space is not a magic wand for protein crystallization but it is a valuable tool for crystallogenesis studies.
crystallogenesis experiments performed in space have contributed to prepare crystals with higher quality than crystals grown in the ground.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystal quality of the space grown crystals was superior to that of ground-grown crystals.
crystals grown in low diffusivities are of higher quality than crystals grown in standard crystallization experiments.
crystallogenesis is not only about the protein itself but it also includes the protein environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physical properties of the crystals can be improved by controlling the crystallization environment, and that this can be done in a reproducible way.
crystallogenesis is not only a matter of crystallizing proteins in a variety of conditions.
the physical quality of protein crystal is not only determined by the quality of the protein itself but also depends on the conditions used to grow the crystals.
